discovery: Geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University, Israel and Chapman University, USA

subfield: Quantum physics / mesoscopic and condensed matter physics
motivation: Aharonov (with the late Bohm) showed in 1959 that electromagnetic potentials have physical effects on electrons in field-free regions. Berry showed in 1984 that any quantum system carried adiabatically around a closed loop acquires a geometric phase that depends only on the geometry of parameter space. Together these insights reshaped our understanding of the quantum wavefunction. Experiments in mesoscopic rings have confirmed Aharonov-Bohm interference. The Berry phase and Berry curvature now underpin the theory of the quantum Hall effects, graphene's anomalous Landau levels, the anomalous Hall effect, topological insulators and polarization in solids, and they inform topological protection in quantum technologies. Berry's semiclassical work on quantum chaos, including Berry-Tabor statistics and random waves, deepens this legacy. This is fundamental theory that unifies disparate phenomena and has been verified across atomic, optical and condensed-matter physics.
